The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ff5a08aaa3d9ad23), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. statement: Let X be a smooth connected pro- jective complex variety whose anticanonical bundle has a smooth Hermitian metric of semipositive Chern curvature. There are a connected finite étale cover ν : S → X, an integer a ≥ 0, and smooth connected projective varieties F and Z with the following properties. 1. For a suitable Kähler metric on X, the common universal cover of X and S has a holomorphic isometric decomposition e X = Ca × F × Z. (2.1) The compact factors are simply connected. The induced metric on F is Ricci-flat, and KF has a nowhere-zero parallel holomorphic section. The anticanonical bundle of Z is smoothly semipositive, and H0 (Z, Ωp Z) = 0 (p > 0), Hq (Z, OZ) = 0 (q > 0). (2.2) The variety Z is rationally connected when it has positive dimension. 2. There are a full lattice Λ ⊂ Ca and a homomorphism ρ : Λ → Aut(Z) for which S = (Ca × F × Z)/Λ, λ · (z, f, v) = (z + λ, f, ρ(λ)v). (2.3) The closure T of ρ(Λ) in the holomorphic isometry group of Z is a compact connected real torus. The trivial torus is allowed. 3. The action of T extends to an algebraic action of a complex algebraic torus G on Z, with T Zariski dense in G. On K−1 Z = det TZ the action is the natural one induced by the differential. For every m ≥ 0, its representation on sections satisfies H0 (Z, K−m Z )T = H0 (Z, K−m Z )G . (2.4) 4. The canonical bundles of Ca and F have nowhere-zero holomorphic frames η0 and ηF invariant under Λ. For every integer m ≥ 0, the product projections pr0, prF , and prZ give the natural, Λ-equivariant identification K−m e X = pr∗ 0 K−m Ca ⊗ pr∗ F K−m F ⊗ pr∗ Z K−m Z , (2.5) in which the first two factors have the invariant frame η−m 0 ⊗ η−m F . Any of the factors may be a point. A point contributes the canonical frame 1; if a = 0, the lattice is the zero group.
